meta.title: How tracking works
meta.subtitle: What a tracking number is, why the page needs no login, and what a scan does and does not prove

sections.title: The tracking number is the credential
sections.narrative:
A recipient has no account and will never make one. They arrive from an SMS, look at one parcel, and leave. So the tracking number itself is what grants access [[track.number-is-credential]], and everything about the endpoint follows from accepting that.

It is sixteen characters [[track.sixteen-chars]] and the endpoint answers *not found* identically for a malformed number, an unknown number, and a number that does not exist [[track.uniform-404]] — telling them apart would make the number space enumerable one request at a time. Requests are rate limited per caller on top of that [[track.rate-limited]].

The response carries nothing that is not already printed on the label [[track.label-only]]. Someone holding the number can already read all of it off the parcel in their hand.

sections.title: What a scan proves, and what it doesn't
sections.narrative:
A scan is evidence that a barcode was read by a device at a moment. That is all it is, and three things follow that surprise people reading this data for the first time.

**The time can be wrong.** `scanned_at` is the handheld's clock [[scans.device-clock]]. A device that has been offline in a depot basement for six hours may also have drifted.

**The order is not arrival order.** Batches upload late, so a scan can land after ones that happened later [[scans.late-arrival]]. A tracking history is ordered by when things happened, not by when Relay heard about them.

**A quiet parcel is not a stopped parcel.** Ten days without a scan marks it lost [[parcel.lost-after-ten-days]], but the gap before that is ordinary — a parcel on a trunk vehicle overnight is scanned at neither end until it arrives.

sections.title: What a recipient can change
sections.narrative:
Rescheduling and redirecting both need a one-time code [[change.needs-otp]], because both change where a parcel physically goes and the tracking number alone is a number printed on a box that everyone who handled it has seen.

Neither is accepted once the parcel is out for delivery that day [[change.not-when-loaded]] — the van is already loaded and sequenced, and the driver is still holding the stop.
